What if you popped every blister?
Blisters are super common after a long walk or a new pair of shoes. It's so tempting. It forms when skin rubs again and again, like new shoes on your heel.

But here's the twist. The fluid and the skin on top protect the raw skin underneath, so popping it can let germs in. Leave it alone and cover it with a bandage! If a big one pops on its own, wash it gently and keep the skin flap on. If it gets red, warm or full of pus, that can mean an infection, so see a doctor.
